summary: Dr. Satya Nitta introduces Emergence as an R&D-driven AI company focused on advancing the science and development of AI agents. The team comprises veterans from leading AI labs including IBM Research, Google Brain, Alexa, Meta, and Microsoft, with a track record of deploying some of the most scaled AI systems on the planet, such as IBM Watson, Alexa, and backend recommendation engines for Amazon Prime, Amazon Video, Twitter, and Bright. Emergence positions itself as a distributed systems meets AI R&D team whose goal is to enable builders to create agents that transform the world. The company is focused on enterprise because enterprise workflows are the most interesting and will stress and push the limits of what autonomous AI can do. Emergence is building two infrastructural platforms. The first is the Orchestrator, a meta-agent that completes the agentic loop of planning, acting, and verifying, remembers and improves over time, and orchestrates across multiple agents and LLMs (both commercial and open source) with appropriate guardrails. It includes a developer dashboard for analyzing prompts, optimizing cost and latency, creating new models with user data, and enhancing existing ones, with the promise that solutions are future-proof and can migrate to the latest LLMs on demand. The Orchestrator is scheduled for GA in August, with early access already live. The second platform is Agent E, an open-source web agent developed in Emergence's R&D labs, designed to learn how to autonomously operate the web and automate complex workflows. Agent E currently tops the Web Voyager Benchmark and is described as the best web agent on the planet. A video demo shows Agent E handling a restaurant reservation request for 15 people with cuisine preferences and sending details to a contact. Emergence's R&D focus centers on self-improvement agents as a core theme, advancing AI planning and reasoning, and solving how agents should be stitched together through agent-oriented programming, all in the context of enterprise workflows like RPA, document processing, and claims processing.

sections.title: Introduction to Emergence and Team Background
sections.summary: Satya Nitta introduces Emergence as an R&D AI company advancing the science and development of agents. The team draws from top AI labs (IBM Research, Google Brain, Alexa, Meta, Microsoft) and has built large-scale AI deployments including IBM Watson, Alexa, and recommendation engines for Amazon Prime, Amazon Video, Twitter, and Bright. Emergence positions itself as a distributed systems meets AI R&D team.

sections.title: Vision for AI Agents in Enterprise
sections.summary: Nitta describes the long-promised vision of AI performing actions for humans, now becoming reality. Emergence focuses on enterprise because enterprise workflows are the most interesting and push the limits of autonomous AI. The company is building two infrastructural platforms to enable this future.

sections.title: The Orchestrator Agent
sections.summary: The Orchestrator is an agent that completes the agentic loop of planning, acting, and verifying, remembers and improves over time, and orchestrates across multiple agents and LLMs with guardrails. It targets enterprise workflows like claims processing. GA is planned for August with early access already live.

sections.title: Agent E: Open-Source Web Agent
sections.summary: Agent E is an open-source web agent developed in Emergence's R&D labs, designed to control the web like a human. It currently tops the Web Voyager Benchmark and is described as the best web agent on the planet. It is built to work seamlessly with the Orchestrator for enterprise workflows.

sections.title: Video Demo and Conclusion
sections.summary: A video demo shows the Orchestrator's developer dashboard for prompt analysis and cost optimization, and Agent E handling a restaurant reservation for 15 people. Nitta concludes by describing Emergence's R&D focus on self-improvement agents, AI planning and reasoning, and agent-oriented programming, applied to enterprise workflows like RPA and document processing.
